entries.title: Prompt visibility command is under-specified
entries.description: The acceptance gate depends on `codex debug prompt-input --profile project_orchestrator`, but the spec does not say how that command is pointed at the generated temporary root or generated config. Because tests must not mutate `~/.codex` or `~/agentic_os`, an implementer could accidentally validate the user's live profile, or validate nothing relevant while the generated `PROFILE.md` remains unloaded.

entries.title: Prompt-file stitching target is not named
entries.description: The spec says to add `PROFILE.md` to whatever generated prompt-file inventory or stitching convention the repo uses, with fallback to `CONTEXT.md` or `AGENTS.md`. That leaves the core invariant dependent on implementer discovery rather than a named code path, so one agent may update only YAML `prompt_files` while another patches the actual loader.

entries.title: Customer safety denylist is too vague
entries.description: Customer artifacts must not contain Genome-private terms, private paths, or unauthorized MCP names, but the spec does not enumerate which terms and MCP identifiers are forbidden or which MCPs are allowed. This makes the customer safety test easy to satisfy superficially while still leaking internal wording or accidentally removing valid customer terminology.

entries.title: Profile compatibility decision remains circular
entries.description: The spec says not to keep duplicate profile names unless current tests prove a public profile name is used, but it does not require the implementer to inspect the existing generated profile names before renaming `project` to `project_orchestrator`. This can break users who invoke existing profile names manually while still passing new tests that only assert the new canonical names.

entries.title: Sidecar YAML conflict ownership is unclear
entries.description: The spec says `config/codex-profile.yml` follows the same managed-file conflict behavior as `config.toml`, but it does not say how generated ownership is detected for new sidecars and `PROFILE.md`. If a user already has a local `PROFILE.md`, implementation could either overwrite it as generated or block forever with no upgrade path.

entries.title: Customer denylist conflicts with managed metadata
entries.description: The spec requires generated sidecars to include `managed_by: genomes_agentic_os`, while the customer safety section frames `config/codex-profile.yml` as part of the generated-artifact denylist surface and later says customer generated files must not include denylisted terms. Although one bullet narrows `genomes_agentic_os` to user-visible role text, the required targeted test says to scan customer generated files, which can make the sidecar both required and forbidden. Implementation agents may either remove required ownership metadata from customer sidecars or weaken the customer scan inconsistently.
